keyTakeaways: Halloween in Japan is an adult costume night with no trick-or-treating tradition; the commercial boom dates from 1997, when Tokyo Disneyland and Kawasaki Halloween both began.
Shibuya's Halloween peak on Center Gai fell from about 40,000 people in 2019 to about 15,000 in 2023, after the ward asked visitors not to come.
Since 1 October 2024, drinking outdoors in central Shibuya has been banned from 6pm to 5am every day of the year.

faqs.question: Do kids go trick-or-treating in Japan?
faqs.answer: Generally no. Japan never had a door-to-door Halloween custom, so the night is about costumes, parades, theme parks and parties for young adults rather than collecting sweets from neighbours.

faqs.question: When did Halloween start in Japan?
faqs.answer: Costume parades ran in Harajuku from 1983 and in Ebisu and Daikanyama from 1987, but the commercial boom dates from 1997, when Tokyo Disneyland began a Halloween event and Kawasaki Halloween started. Many travel guides say 2000; a 2025 Waseda study's newspaper-based timeline puts it at 1997.

faqs.question: Can you still go to Shibuya on Halloween?
faqs.answer: You can, but the ward has asked people not to come since 2023 and closed the square in front of the Hachiko statue that year. Expect heavy policing, and keep moving rather than stopping in the crowd.

faqs.question: Is drinking on the street allowed in Shibuya?
faqs.answer: Not at night. Since 1 October 2024, drinking outdoors in central Shibuya has been banned from 6pm to 5am every day of the year. There is no legal penalty, but security officers may confiscate drinks.

faqs.question: Is the Kawasaki Halloween parade still held?
faqs.answer: No. Kawasaki Halloween ran from 1997 and its organisers announced its end in 2021. Older travel guides that still recommend it are out of date.

faqs.question: Is Halloween a public holiday in Japan?
faqs.answer: No. It is an imported, commercial event rather than a national holiday, so 31 October is an ordinary working or school day unless it falls on a weekend, as it does in 2026 and 2027.

faqs.question: What day is Halloween in Japan in 2026 and 2027?
faqs.answer: Halloween is 31 October every year. It falls on Saturday 31 October 2026 and Sunday 31 October 2027.

faqs.question: Can I wear my Halloween costume on the train in Japan?
faqs.answer: Nothing in the sources we checked forbids it, but bulky costumes are awkward on packed trains, and Halloween train parties needed police at Shinjuku Station back in 1992. Changing at the venue is the considerate choice.

faqs.question: What is the Japanese word for Halloween?
faqs.answer: It is ハロウィン, pronounced harowin, a loanword from English. Some writers use the longer spelling ハロウィーン, which you may also see on posters and packaging.

faqs.question: Does Japan have its own festival for the dead?
faqs.answer: Yes, Obon, held in mid-August. Families return home to clean graves and welcome their ancestors, and towns hold Bon dances. It is a family occasion at home, not a costume night.

faqs.question: What time is it in Japan when it's evening in India?
faqs.answer: Japan is three and a half hours ahead of India, because Japan Standard Time is UTC+9 and Indian Standard Time is UTC+5:30. At 7pm in Delhi it is 10:30pm in Tokyo.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween in Japan: Adult Costumes, Big Crowds and New Rules

Halloween in Japan is a costume night for young adults, not a children's door-to-door ritual: there is no trick-or-treating tradition, and the holiday spread as a commercial event from the late 1990s. A [2025 Waseda University study of Shibuya Halloween by Yushi Sugiura](https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/lifology/46/0/46_1/_article/-char/en) dates the turning point to 1997, when Tokyo Disneyland and the Kawasaki Halloween parade both began. It is no public holiday in Japan; the next dates are Saturday 31 October 2026, then Sunday 31 October 2027.

Messaging a friend there instead? Across all SubhSandesh templates, not Halloween alone, 48.3% of the views a shared page gets come from phones, and a typical page collects 11.1 views.

The biggest street gathering has been shrinking on purpose. The peak crowd on Shibuya's Center Gai fell from about 40,000 in 2019 to about 15,000 in 2023, and drinking on the street near the station is now banned from 6pm to 5am all year.

## What is Halloween in Japan, and who celebrates it?

Halloween in Japan (ハロウィン, *harowin*) is an imported autumn event centred on dressing up, held on and around 31 October. Young adults wear costumes to theme parks, bars, parades and city streets, and there is no door-to-door custom for children to join.

Sugiura observed Shibuya around 31 October every year from 2013 to 2023 and interviewed people there in 2016, 2017 and 2022. Participants came as individuals or small friend groups, never as neighbourhood teams, and one had simply stopped on the way home from a Disney Halloween event.

### Why costumes matter more than candy

Japan already had a large cosplay scene, so Halloween slotted into a habit that existed. In Sugiura's account, anyone in the Shibuya crowd can buy a costume nearby and switch from spectator to performer, with no permit and no organiser, while photographs from strangers work as the reward. By 2020 similar street gatherings had appeared in Osaka, Nagoya and Fukuoka.

## How did Halloween catch on in Japan? A dated timeline

English-language travel guides usually date Halloween's arrival to 2000. Sugiura's timeline, compiled from newspaper archives, runs earlier.

### 1983–1992: parades and train parties

A Halloween parade at the Kiddy Land shop in Harajuku in 1983 is often called Japan's first. Local merchants took it over in 1990 and were still running it in 2023, and a parade in Ebisu and Daikanyama has run since 1987.

In 1992 foreign residents commandeered carriages on the Yamanote Line for a Halloween party, and police were sent to Shinjuku Station. The Yomiuri Shimbun reported similar train parties again in 1997.

### 1997: Tokyo Disneyland and Kawasaki

Tokyo Disneyland started its Halloween event in 1997, the same year Citta Entertainment, which runs a shopping and entertainment complex in Kawasaki, launched Kawasaki Halloween. Sugiura reads this as post-bubble retail strategy: October needed an event to bridge the summer Obon holidays and the Christmas shopping season.

Kawasaki Halloween is now history. Its organisers announced its end in 2021, which several travel guides still miss.

### 2007–2017: Shibuya becomes the stage

Street gatherings at Shibuya Crossing took shape around 2007, after New Year countdowns from 2000 and World Cup celebrations in 2002 had made the junction a place to gather. By 2014 riot police were directing traffic, and in 2015 the ward set up temporary cloakrooms and toilets for costumed visitors.

From 2016 police closed roads and turned them into pedestrian zones on Halloween night. Ikebukuro, meanwhile, had begun its own Halloween cosplay festival in 2014.

## What happened to Shibuya Halloween?

The ward moved from hosting the crowd to discouraging it in about five years. After revellers overturned a truck in 2018, Shibuya asked shops to stop selling alcohol in bottles, and in 2019 an ordinance restricted street drinking around the station during Halloween.

In 2020 the mayor asked people to stay away because of COVID-19, and the cloakrooms and toilets were discontinued. Sugiura cites a Nikkei report that the ward's security spending had passed ¥100 million in its heaviest years.

### Why Seoul's 2022 crowd crush changed Japan's response

On 29 October 2022 a crowd crush in Seoul's Itaewon district killed more than 150 people during Halloween gatherings. A [2024 PLOS ONE reconstruction by Liang and colleagues](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC11244771) estimated average density in the alley at 7.57 people per square metre, peaking at 9.95, and named the causes as a large crowd, two streams colliding head-on, and escalating panic.

Shibuya's 2023 response was its firmest yet. The ward asked people not to come, closed the square in front of the Hachiko statue, and enforced its bans on street drinking and smoking. The mayor reported a peak of about 15,000 people on Center Gai at around 10pm on Halloween night, against roughly 23,000 in 2022 and 40,000 in 2019.

From 1 October 2024 the drinking restriction became year-round. [Time Out Tokyo reported on 4 October 2024](https://www.timeout.com/tokyo/news/public-drinking-is-now-banned-at-shibuya-every-day-all-year-round-100424) that outdoor drinking is banned from 6pm to 5am daily across central Shibuya, including Center Street, Miyashita Park and Maruyamacho. There is no legal penalty, but patrols were stepped up and private security officers may confiscate drinks.

## How is Halloween different from Obon?

Obon is Japan's own festival of returning spirits, and it falls in mid-August rather than at the end of October. Families travel back to the family home to clean graves, decorate the household altar and welcome the ancestors, and towns hold Bon dances around a central platform.

A [2024 PLOS ONE study of the Bon festival in Mikasa, Hokkaido by Irving and colleagues](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC10956785) surveyed 183 festival participants. Belief in ancestors was consistently associated with stronger social cohesion, and dancing actively was linked to closer feelings towards other attendees.

That contrast explains a lot about Japanese Halloween. Obon is about family, home and the dead, while Halloween is about strangers, streets and dressing up, so the two do not compete for the same role.

## Halloween in Japan at a glance

The table compares the events most guides mention, with the year each status was last confirmed in a dated source. Schedules change every autumn, so check the organiser's own calendar for the year you travel.

| Event or place | What happens | Status (verified year) | Visitor tip |
|---|---|---|---|
| Harajuku–Omotesando parade | Merchant-run costume parade, first held in 1983 | Still running in 2023 | Check the merchants' association notice for the date |
| Tokyo Disneyland Halloween | Seasonal Halloween event at the park | Started 1997; check the park calendar each year | The park sets its own costume rules; read them before packing |
| Kawasaki Halloween | Organised costume parade with a participation fee | Ran 1997–2021; ended 2021 | Do not plan a trip around it |
| Shibuya Crossing street gathering | Unofficial costume crowd since about 2007 | Ward asks people not to come (2023); drinking banned 6pm–5am year-round (2024) | Watch briefly and keep moving with the flow |
| Ikebukuro cosplay festival | Organised cosplay event | Started 2014 | The organised option if costumes are the point |

The pattern is clear: events with an owner have lasted, while the ownerless street crowd is being managed down. Most English-language guides still frame Shibuya the other way round.

## What should visitors know about Halloween in Japan?

Halloween 2026 lands on a Saturday, which pushes weekend crowds and Halloween night together. Halloween 2027 is a Sunday, the night before a working Monday.

A few habits keep the night easy. Most come straight from the history above.

- Change into elaborate costumes at the venue rather than on crowded trains; train parties drew police as early as 1992.
- Do not drink on the street in central Shibuya between 6pm and 5am, on any day.
- Avoid narrow lanes where people are moving in both directions, the pattern behind the Itaewon crush.
- Carry your rubbish with you; litter has drawn complaints since at least 2015, when a dawn clean-up of Shibuya began the morning after Halloween.
- Check Shibuya ward and police notices in the week before Halloween, as closures change year to year.

Japan Standard Time is UTC+9, three and a half hours ahead of India. Evening in Tokyo is afternoon in Delhi, which matters if you are timing a message to a friend there.

## Sending Halloween wishes to a friend in Japan

When your best friend spends the season in Tokyo, a link that lands on their phone suits the night better than a parcel that turns up in November. The [interactive Halloween card](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) includes a bestie setting that rewrites its final question and licence for a friend. You supply a letter, up to half a dozen photos and the word for the jack-o'-lantern; your friend raps on a tiny haunted house's door, carves until the candle catches, then opens your letter by flashlight up in a darkened attic.

For the letter itself, here are a few original lines for a friend abroad. Keep one, or use them as a starting point.

- "You found the one country where Halloween is all costume and no candy. Send photos."
- "Three and a half hours ahead of me and still the last to leave the party."
- "Tell Shibuya I said behave. Tell yourself the same."

For a reveal at a particular hour Japan time, the [premium Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) lets you set an unlock moment. Before it arrives your friend sees just their name above a countdown, and the page can carry a voice message of 60 seconds at most. Platform-wide, 38.5% of creators also add a password before sharing.

### When a link is not the right Halloween greeting

Both pages run in English only, so a Japanese-speaking friend who reads little English may prefer a handwritten card. Each page greets one person and is no group invitation, and if you are in Japan together, a costume and a night out beat any link.

## Sources

- Sugiura, Y. (2025). [Modern Characteristics of Urban Festivals in Shibuya Halloween: Study of a Visitor-Driven Celebration](https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/lifology/46/0/46_1/_article/-char/en). *Journal of Lifology*, 46, 1–14. Published 31 March 2025.
- Liang, H., Lee, S., Sun, J. and Wong, S.C. (2024). [Unraveling the causes of the Seoul Halloween crowd-crush disaster](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC11244771). *PLOS ONE*, 19(7). Published 12 July 2024.
- Irving, B., Kavanagh, C., Fischer, R. and Yuki, M. (2024). [Dance for the dead: top-down beliefs, social cohesion and anxiety in collective rituals](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC10956785). *PLOS ONE*. Published 21 March 2024.
- Nagao, S. (2024). [Public drinking is now banned in Shibuya every day, all year round](https://www.timeout.com/tokyo/news/public-drinking-is-now-banned-at-shibuya-every-day-all-year-round-100424). *Time Out Tokyo*. Published 4 October 2024.
